RFC 9999: Structured Context Framing Protocol

Status of this Memo: This document specifies an Internet Standards Track protocol for structured context exchange between autonomous agents and conversational gateways.

1. Introduction

Real-time conversational agents require reliable context encapsulation to maintain multi-turn coherence across heterogeneous transport layers. This specification defines the frame boundaries, header formatting, and serialization invariants necessary for bidirectional agent streaming.

2. Frame Structure

Each message frame MUST begin with a 4-byte magic delimiter followed by a 16-bit payload length descriptor. Payloads exceeding the maximum negotiated transmission unit (MTU) MUST be partitioned into sequential chunk frames with monotonic sequence numbering.
